department: Graduate School in Physics, Department of Physics and Astronomy

deadline.value: No central deadline: doctoral positions are advertised under Vacant positions throughout the year, each with its own deadline
deadline.quote: Doctoral student positions are publicly announced and listed under Vacant positions. New positions are posted regularly throughout the year.

gre_subject.value: Not stated on the page checked

supervisor.value: Not stated on the page checked

funding.value: Doctoral students are employed by Chalmers on a monthly salary (fixed-term, generally at most five years), with up to 20% teaching or departmental work
funding.quote: As a doctoral student, you are employed by Chalmers. | Doctoral students are employed with a monthly salary, and doctoral programmes incur no fees. | Teaching and other departmental work may account for a maximum of 20 per cent of working hours.

entry_route.value: A completed master's degree (60 or 120 credits) with a specialisation close enough to the subject, plus the graduate school's subject-specific requirements
entry_route.quote: To be admitted to doctoral programmes at Chalmers, you must have completed a degree at second-cycle level, i.e. a Master’s degree with 120 higher education credits or a Master’s degree with 60 higher education credits. | Your degree should also have a specialisation that is sufficiently related to the subject of the doctoral programme.

app_fee.value: No fees: Chalmers states that doctoral programmes incur no fees
app_fee.quote: Doctoral students are employed with a monthly salary, and doctoral programmes incur no fees.

notes: The Graduate School in Physics is run by the Department of Physics and Astronomy. Its syllabus sections (including entry requirements) are collapsed on the page and did not appear in the text checked, so the rules above are Chalmers-wide. Licentiate after about two years; doctorate after four to five years.
